findings.message: Erasure only checks whether the person's own ids or name are under a hold. It ignores matter holds on the rows it is about to change. `place_legal_hold` says a hold pauses 'the purge and erasure' for a matter's records, and the purge honours it through `notHeld()`, but `erase()` calls `applyRule(tx, rule, about(rule, who))` with no hold filter. Fix: AND the erase condition with `notHeld(rule, held)`, use the same filter for the included name-only rows, and list held rows as kept in the inventory.
findings.scenario: A matter hold is placed with ids=[project X id]. An erasure for Kasun is then approved. The time.entry rows with user_id=kasun and project_id=X have note and logged_by anonymised, even though they are under the hold.

findings.message: Several new retention entries list a personal column in `fields` but not in `subject` or `subjectName`. Requests and holds find rows only through those two lists. Missed: time.week.decided_by, time.entry.logged_by and presales.opportunity.lead_name. When the erased person is the approver, logger or lead, their rows are neither erased nor exported, and holds don't protect them. Fix: add each person column to `subject`, or to `subjectName` for names, and add a test that erases an approver.
findings.scenario: Sahan approved 40 timesheet weeks (time.week.decided_by = Sahan). Sahan's erasure request completes as 'Erased', but those 40 rows still hold decided_by for Sahan, and Sahan's access package leaves them out.

findings.message: `nameRows` lists at most 500 rows per rule (LIMIT). `decideNameRows` checks the decision against those listed rows only, then replaces the review item (whose n counts every row) with the included and excluded listed rows. Rows past 500 are never listed, never decided, never acted on, and drop out of the inventory without a trace, so the request completes. Fix: refuse to complete, or page through the rows, when the count is above the limit, and keep the unlisted rows as a review item.
findings.scenario: There are 620 presales.task rows with owner_name 'Rizwan Farook'. The approver decides the 500 listed rows. The request completes as 'Erased', and 120 rows are untouched and missing from the stored inventory.

findings.message: A person hold copies `resolveSubject` ids into `legal_hold.subjects` when it is placed. Ids the person gains afterwards are not held. A fix in this diff re-resolves ids for erasure requests for exactly this reason, but holds still use the old snapshot. Fix: for kind='person', store the user id and re-resolve the person's ids in `held()` on each purge or erasure.
findings.scenario: A hold is placed on Ivy. HR then creates a new hr.person and employment row for her rehire. Once due, the purge anonymises the new hr.employment bank fields (subject person_id = new id), because held.ids doesn't contain that id.

findings.message: `countsAsPage` skips any request that carries a prefetch header or a `next-action` header. The client sets all of these headers. The proxy comment says skipping `rsc: 1` would let clients dodge the limit, but these headers allow the same bypass. A GET with `next-action` or `purpose: prefetch` still renders the page. Fix: exempt `next-action` only on POST, and count prefetches (at lower weight or in their own bucket) rather than not at all.
findings.scenario: A script sends GET /delivery with the header `purpose: prefetch` 10,000 times a minute. Every request returns 200, and none reach the 600/min page limit or api.rate_limited.

findings.message: Erasure anonymises every field of a rule on any row whose subject matches. `allocations.allocation` lists `person_id` as a subject and `updated_by` as the field, and `time.week` lists `user_id` as a subject with `decided_by` as a field. Erasing an employee therefore wipes the attribution of the PM or approver, which breaks the rule that every record says who did it. It also leaves the employee's own reference (`person_id`) in place. Fix: limit each rule's fields to the subject columns that matched, or split the rules per person column.
findings.scenario: Erasing Nimal sets updated_by to null on every allocation of Nimal that Maya made. The record no longer shows that Maya made the change, and Nimal's person_id is still there.

findings.message: `failure()` maps only CallerError, RateLimitedError, ToolError, Forbidden/Scope, ValidationError and errors with code not_found or invalid_input. PrivacyError and other domain refusals have no code, so they return 500 'internal' and are logged as server faults. Fix: map errors with `retryable === false` to 400 or 409 with their message.
findings.scenario: POST /api/v1/tools/set_retention_period {rule:'Incoming webhook calls', period:'P1D'} returns 500 {error:'internal'} instead of a 400 saying the period can't go below P90D. Clients retry it as a server fault.

findings.message: The tool's period regex `^P(\d+[YMWD])+$` disagrees with the service's `^P(\d+Y)?(\d+M)?(\d+W)?(\d+D)?$` and with the DB check. The tool accepts 'P1M1Y', which the service then rejects. Use one exported schema.
findings.scenario: period 'P6M1Y' passes the tool's validation, then fails in the service with a validation error.

findings.message: The fixture computes subject_key with a plain sha256 of the user id. The service uses `keyed(s.userId)`. The two copies disagree, so any lookup by subject_key misses the seeded request. Call `keyed()` here.
A delivery that egress refuses (NonRetryableError, one attempt) is recorded with attempts = RETRY.maxAttempts. Record the real attempt count from the failed step.
findings.scenario: A webhook host that resolves to 10.0.0.5 gets a delivery row with attempts=5, although only one attempt was made.

findings.message: api.webhook holds a personal `created_by` column (and so do privacy.retention_period.set_by and privacy.legal_hold.placed_by), but no retention entry covers it. Requests and holds can't find these rows. Add entries to apiRetention and to privacyOwn.
SCREENS gained `settings/api` but not `settings/retention`, so the new retention screen is not covered by the no-write-form check.
The proxy-order test greps the source of proxy.ts rather than driving the proxy, so it doesn't prove that page requests are limited. Drive the proxy handler instead.

The limiter's counts live in each process's memory. On Vercel and Cloudflare, every instance and isolate keeps its own counts, so the effective limit is the configured limit times the number of instances. The README notes this, but the screen shows the configured figure as enforced.

The token endpoint advertises client_credentials with `client_secret_post` only. RFC 6749 requires HTTP Basic client authentication, and `exchangeClientCredentials` reads only the form body. Support or advertise `client_secret_basic`.
The read tools build their context with source hard-coded to "chat", whatever the real channel (mcp or api). Pass the tool's `source` through.

The access package caps each section, and the audit list, at 5000 rows with `limit 5000`. Nothing records that a section was cut short, so the package presents itself as the person's complete data. Fix: count the rows first, then either page through them or mark the section as truncated and refuse to complete the request.
findings.scenario: An engineer has 7 years of time.entry rows (more than 5000). The access request completes and the package holds 5000 entries, with no sign that the rest are missing.

findings.message: This round fixed the 'no secret set up' case for incoming webhooks (`not_configured` is a setup problem, not an attacker) but not for outgoing ones. If the tenant has no `amax-webhook` signing secret, `useSecret` throws on every attempt. The delivery is retried, recorded as a receiver failure and added to `failures`. After `MAX_FAILURES` events the webhook is switched off, and the screen tells the admin to fix the receiver. `subscribeWebhook` does not check that the secret exists either. Fix: refuse to subscribe when the signing secret is missing, and treat `SecretNotConfiguredError` at delivery as a non-retryable setup error that does not count toward switch-off.
findings.scenario: A tenant with no amax-webhook secret subscribes a healthy receiver. After 5 events it shows 'Switched off' with 'The X webhook was switched off after failing', and nothing was ever sent.

findings.message: GitHub and Microsoft Graph calls carry no signed timestamp, so the `api.inbound` dedupe row is their only replay protection, as the comment here says. The purge still deletes those rows after the P90D `minimum`. After that, a captured signed GitHub delivery or Graph notification verifies again and is accepted as new. The dedupe key is a body hash, not personal data. Fix: keep the dedupe hashes of verified rows with no time-based delete (for example, a separate non-personal table), or tie GitHub and Graph acceptance to a freshness field inside the signed body.
findings.scenario: An attacker captures a signed GitHub push on day 0. On day 91 the purge has deleted the dedupe row. Replaying the same headers and body gives verifyWebhook ok and receiveWebhook ok:true, so the event is processed again.

findings.message: Rate-limited counts are held in memory and written only by a `setTimeout` five seconds later. On Vercel and Cloudflare, where the proxy runs in its own function or worker, the instance is often frozen or recycled before the timer fires. Those 429s are never written to `api.rate_limited`, and the screen shows 'None this week'. Requests that were limited read as no limiting. Fix: write the count in the request path (a `waitUntil`/`after()` hook on the proxy or route) or flush synchronously when a 429 is answered.
findings.scenario: On Vercel a user hits the page limit and gets a 429. The function instance is suspended within 5 s. api.rate_limited gets no row, and the 'Requests rate-limited' tile shows 0.
